headline: HMSI pivots to dealer margins and buyer retention over market share
hook: Volume takes a back seat at HMSI
summary: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India is prioritizing dealer profitability and long-term customer retention over chasing annual volume rankings and pure market share. President and CEO Tsutsumu Otani stated that the strategy emphasizes expanding vehicles in operation to protect the dealer network. During April-October, HMSI domestic dispatches reached 3.7 million units, trailing Hero MotoCorp at 4.0 million units. The company also aims to tap new growth by increasing female participation in personal mobility, which currently accounts for 10% of its business.
why_it_matters: Dealer health prioritized over volume growth in the two-wheeler market.

summary: Hero MotoCorp reports that its Vida electric scooter range incurs annual electricity costs of ₹1,564 under specific usage conditions. The company saw a 114.5% year-on-year increase in electric scooter sales during October 2026. This data highlights the operational cost efficiency of the brand's EV portfolio as it competes in the growing Indian electric two-wheeler market.
why_it_matters: Lower running costs may boost Hero's electric vehicle market share.

headline: Hero MotoCorp secures ITAT relief on Rs 27 crore tax demand across six assessment years
hook: Tax relief of Rs27 crore for Hero

modes.simple: Hero MotoCorp won an appeal against a tax bill of Rs 27 crore from the government, saving the company from paying that amount.

summary: Hero MotoCorp announced in a regulatory filing that it has received favorable appeal orders from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) portal regarding a tax demand of Rs 27 crore covering six assessment years. The company downloaded the order dated November 20, 2026, on the same day. For an Indian retail investor, this removes a potential contingent tax liability for the two-wheeler maker. The resolution of legacy tax disputes clears regulatory overhang for the company.
why_it_matters: Tax overhang lifted for Hero MotoCorp.
winners_losers: Hero MotoCorp gains / tax authorities hurt

headline: Understanding the hidden costs in low-priced electric scooters

modes.bear: Hidden subscription costs may lead to consumer dissatisfaction and regulatory scrutiny regarding transparent pricing practices in the EV industry.
modes.bull: Battery-as-a-service models lower the initial barrier to entry, potentially accelerating mass-market EV adoption and increasing total addressable market size.
modes.simple: When buying an electric scooter, the advertised price often doesn't include the battery. You might have to pay a monthly fee to use it, which changes the real cost of the vehicle.

summary: Several electric scooter manufacturers, including TVS, Ola, Hero, Ampere, and e-Sprinto, are marketing entry-level prices as low as ₹49,999. These headline figures often exclude the cost of the battery, which is instead offered through separate subscription or rental plans. Consumers must account for these recurring battery costs to determine the true total cost of ownership. This distinction is critical for retail investors tracking the adoption rates and revenue models of the Indian EV sector.
why_it_matters: Low sticker prices may hide higher long-term battery subscription costs.
